# Stimpunks.World

> Queer without fear. Interdependent and here. Divergent and proud. Living out loud. Plucky pluralism, for human organisms. Becoming and belonging, with ribald songing.

A Stimpunks Foundation site, and the loud one. It has no single design system on purpose: the street is the system and the rooms refuse to share one. Through a gate in the wall there is a garden, with one bed for every site we publish and every bed linking out to it. The street has an edge at each end and they are not the same kind of edge: past the treeline there is a campground, for anybody who would rather not be on a street at all, and past the last streetlight the other way there is a road out of town, where the mystical and the after-dark keep premises. Two habits survive from our careful sites — attribution, which is a licence rather than a house style, and contrast, because clashing is not the same as illegible.

Every page carries an intensity dial with three settings. It defaults to whatever the visitor's device asks for and lets them turn it up past that; Gentle removes motion and sparkle and never removes content.

## The rooms, the garden through the gate, and the field at the end of the street

- [Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/): Queer without fear. Interdependent and here. Divergent and proud. Living out loud. One street, no two rooms alike, a garden through the gate in the wall, a campground past the treeline, and a dial that lets you decide how loud it gets. A Stimpunks Foundation site.
- [The Map — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/map.html): The whole street as a model in white card on a cutting mat: every shopfront where it stands, the rooms behind rooms, the garden through its gate, the campgrounds past the treeline at one end and the road out past the last streetlight at the other. Pick anything up to go there. Built from the street itself, so it grows when the street does.
- [Danny the Street — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/danny-the-street.html): Where this street got its name. Danny the Street is a sentient street in DC Comics' Doom Patrol, created in 1990 by Grant Morrison and Richard Case, named after the drag performer Danny La Rue, hunted by an agency devoted to normalcy, and played on television as genderqueer. What Danny has been since, and which parts of Danny this site took.
- [Pink Pony Club — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/pink-pony-club.html): The dancefloor. Ten songs our own pages already credit, in one jukebox. Nothing plays until you press play — no autoplay, and nothing reaches YouTube before you ask for it.
- [The Chappell — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/the-chappell.html): A subroom off Pink Pony Club: thirteen Chappell Roan videos in a rhinestone chapel, and the whole playlist at the east end. Every label that plays one thing says how long before you press it, and nothing reaches YouTube until you do.
- [Club Chronic — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/club-chronic.html): Freaks to the front. A punk club on the street: the story of scenes that built their own doors, every playlist we keep, and a rack of records along the back wall. Nothing plays until you press play, and nothing in here strobes.
- [The Zine Table — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/zine-table.html): Xerox, staples, ransom note. The room where we get angry in ten point type — and the room that explains which two things stay careful even here.
- [The Zine Table, Issue #2: One Root, Two Rainbows — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/zine-issue-2.html): Seven lessons on neurodiversity and gender, photocopied down to one sheet. Distilled from our own library, with the course linked and the song left unprinted.
- [Hear Queer Here — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/hear-queer-here.html): Quantum queering: reading queerness and the physics of indeterminacy through each other. Nothing is fixed, bounded, or settled in advance of its relations.
- [Enid's Room — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/enids-room.html): Colorful goth. Black walls, technicolour everything else, and somewhere to sit when the glee runs out. The room for the one who doesn't match the house.
- [The Polaroid Wall — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/polaroids.html): How a photo gets onto Enid's wall, what we ask for, what we promise, and how it comes down again. The wall is empty on purpose until somebody sends one.
- [The Playhouse — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/playhouse.html): Everything is a button and every button yells. The glossary wearing a costume — and every toy is a real control that Tab reaches and a screen reader names.
- [The Arcade — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/arcade.html): A grape carpet, a marquee, and cabinets standing on it. Walk up to one. Nothing in here has a timer, a score, a way to lose or a sound, and nothing in any of them is trying to beat you.
- [Quill Drift — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/quill-drift.html): A cabinet in the Arcade. Esmx the Porkypine walks a dark field and the loose quills drifting across it join their mane on contact. No timer, no lives, no score, nothing to defeat, and nothing you can throw.
- [Otterly Adorbs — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/otterly-adorbs.html): A cabinet in the Arcade. You steer an otter round a kelp bay: twirls, somersaults, dives, floating on your back, and fish at feeding time. Floating fills nothing up, on purpose. No timer, no lives, no score, nothing to defeat.
- [Penguin Pebbling — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/penguin-pebbling.html): A cabinet in the Arcade. A shore, some pebbles, and neighbours with nests. Carry something over and give it to somebody. Nothing is counted, nothing is owed back, and there is no wrong thing to give anybody.
- [The Latibulum — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/latibulum.html): A burrow of belonging for burnouts. Under the hill: a round door, a lamp, a wireless playing ocean waves, a television showing seated tai chi, and a shelf of things to do with a bodymind. Nothing counted, nothing loud, nothing plays until you press play.
- [The Jungle Room — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/jungle-room.html): A viewing room under a closed canopy. The nature live cams our own Watering Hole Hangs page puts on in the background — waterholes, otters, reefs, forests, butterflies, nests and whoever walks past — in that page's own groups and order. Nothing plays until you press play, and nothing here says how long it runs, because none of it ends.
- [The Den — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/the-den.html): Behind the Jungle Room, the other Jungle Room: Elvis Presley's den at Graceland — green shag, carved wood, a fieldstone waterfall — which in 1976 was turned into a recording studio. Sixteen songs cut in that carpet across two sessions, in the order they were recorded, and every one of them says how long it runs before you press it.
- [The Mopery — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/the-mopery.html): A dark academia library, reading room and parlour. Shelves of books that open to a note and a way to borrow them, one screen playing versions of Paint It Black, and a reading nook where The Raven can be set in any face on the street. Nothing plays until you press play.
- [The Oracle Deck — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/oracle-deck.html): Thirteen public domain engravings from the Metropolitan Museum's open collection, each with a question on the back. It asks and does not answer: no fortunes, no reversals, nothing about what is going to happen to you. The whole deck is on the page.
- [The Doomscroll — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/the-doomscroll.html): Public domain poems of doom and gloom, laid out as a feed of bad news, newest first by the date each was first published — on an actual scroll. Every poem is entire, every text names the printing it came from, and every author has been dead more than seventy years.
- [The Adventurer’s Guild — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/adventurers-guild.html): A job board in a manila room, on a street where nothing else is tidy. Each job sends you to a marker standing in one of the rooms; the marker gives you a code, and the code comes back here. Nothing is scored, nothing expires, every job carries hints and a give-me-the-answer way out, and the fanfare does whatever the dial says.
- [The Feed — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/the-feed.html): A split-flap arrivals board in a dark concourse, one wire per site, carrying the latest from stimpunks.org and every one of its sibling sites off their own RSS feeds. A title, a date and where it goes — never the words themselves. The board says the minute it was set, because a board is not the railway.
- [The Zibaldone — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/zibaldone.html): A commonplace book left open on a desk. Quotations copied out by hand for whatever state you are in, every one of them naming the printing it came from and how it was checked. Short quotations only, no song lyrics, and nothing here is ranked.
- [The Rabbit Hole — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/rabbit-hole.html): You meant to look up one thing. A shaft you fall down on purpose: rabbit holing as monotropic attention rather than a failure of discipline, seven recordings off our own glossary entry, six 1865 wood engravings, and a trail out. Nothing plays until you press play.
- [The Healing Checkpoint — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/healing-checkpoint.html): Room 429. A save room off the street with a spring in the floor and a bed nobody is charging you for: an appreciation of rest built out of our own Rest entry, the healing checkpoint as a place that asks nothing, and a Retry-After slip you can send somebody. Nothing here is counted and nothing is stored.
- [The Foundry — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/foundry.html): A type foundry on the street: a grey iron workshop where you can set your own words, or words out of The Playhouse, The Mopery and The Zibaldone, in any typeface this site holds. Size, leading, tracking, measure, weight, a real italic or a machine slant, four measured inks, and a proof you can print with the designer's name on it.
- [Covenstead — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/covenstead.html): A kitchen on the street in the afternoon, with the good china out and none of it matching. Counsel that stayed counsel, a law the tradition itself argues about, and the practice of watching your own first thoughts. Nobody is initiated.
- [Dead Tired Society — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/dead-tired-society.html): Peer support by and for people in burnout, and for the ones on the far side of it. A borrowed room after hours with the big lights off and the door left ajar. Masking, minority stress, epistemic injustice and the rest, hung up on pegs by the door. No advice nobody asked for, nothing counted, and nobody has to sit in the light.
- [Laughingstock — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/laughingstock.html): A comedy club on the street, down a ramp rather than a flight of stairs. Disabled comics on their own terms, in their own voice, controlling the frame: Josh Blue, Tina Friml and the rest of our Disabled Comedy playlist, with the writing from our Campfire Learn Together on why being disabled can be pretty funny. Nobody here is called brave, and bombing is allowed.
- [The Lightbulb Picture House — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/lightbulb-picture-house.html): A picture house on the street where every screening is a relaxed screening: the house lights stay up, the captions are on, and you can move, stim, sit on the floor or leave. Two screens of films about autism, ADHD and neurodiversity, most of them made by the people they are about, and a rack with a card for every film saying how long it runs and what is in it before you press play.
- [Samefood Cafe — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/samefood-cafe.html): A café on the street for samefoods and safe foods, and for understanding food aversion rather than correcting it. The kitchen knows its regulars, keeps what each of them has, and is ready when their samefoods change with the seasons; nothing on your plate touches unless you want it to, Matthew Broberg-Moffitt’s Color Taste Texture is on the counter, and our community’s own samefoods are on trays of their own.
- [The Collection Collection — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/collection-collection.html): A dark gallery on the street full of our people’s collections, each in a cabinet of its own under a lamp of its own, and no two lamps alike: pens, paper and ink, perfume, leather swatches and stamping tools, house plants, books and rocks. Nothing is counted, priced or ranked, and the house describes every photograph so that nobody has to before they send one.
- [Vital Plant Living — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/vital-plant-living.html): A plant-based kitchen on the street. Build your own bowl or wrap out of a real pantry, the list Ryan cooks from at home, or start from one of the named combos on the board, each standing on a flavour base from somewhere in the world; copy what you build and take it shopping. Everything in here is drawn cut through the middle, so everything in the bowl touches, and the stereo plays songs about food.
- [Community Center — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/community-center.html): A shopfront on the street with the blinds half open: the front desk where you sign on to the CB with a handle and this week's password, its house norms and our covenant, and the community service board, with a slot for every room that takes something in from our community.
- [Dopamine Dress-Up Den — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/dopamine-dress-up-den.html): A boutique on the street for dopamine dressing, Helen Edgar's idea. Put an outfit together on a valet stand out of rails of Thai fisherman pants, haori, button-downs, beanies, cardigans, flowing dresses, capes, sequins and a feather boa, in any print and any colours. Nothing has to go with anything, nothing comes in a size, and black is a colour too.
- [Plural Mural — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/plural-mural.html): An end wall on the street with a mural on it, and then another. The street is Danny's, and Danny repaints: at MAX GLITTER the wall dissolves into the next mural every three minutes and you can hold the one you like; at every setting you can put any of them up yourself. The murals are the house's, and anybody can propose one in words.
- [Your Room — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/your-room.html): An empty storefront on the street, with the keys in the door. One person from the community gets a page here, their own stylesheet, and their name on it.
- [The Pebble Board — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/pebble-board.html): A community noticeboard on the street. Our people bring each other songs, art, jokes, recipes and things worth keeping, and one edition at a time gets pinned up here. Nothing plays until you press play.
- [Now Playing — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/now-playing.html): A screenprinted bill pasted on the poster column on the pavement, beside the Pebble Board: every room on this street with something in it to press and play, what is on there, and what each one puts on first. Read off the rooms themselves. Nothing on the poster plays.
- [The Garden — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/the-garden.html): Through the gate in the wall: the knowledge garden, with one bed for every site we publish. What a knowledge garden is, how this one is tended, how to start one of your own, and the Garden Spider, whose best answer is an entrance.
- [The Campgrounds — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/campgrounds.html): Where the street runs out. A field past the treeline with numbered pitches on it, for the ones who would rather live on the edge of town. Nothing out here moves, at any setting.
- [Faery Yurt — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/faery-yurt.html): Helen's candlelit yurt in the campgrounds, pitched at the edge of the woods. Old books, fairy lights, a regulation nook, three animals with opinions, and a window that opens onto somewhere else entirely.
- [Swaying Sweetgrass — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/swaying-sweetgrass.html): Pitch 02 in the campgrounds. A meadow of sweetgrass left alone, with one natural-surface path a wheelchair can use running into a clearing with a fire pit in it. The story at the fire is Robin Wall Kimmerer in her own voice.
- [The Solarpunk Hermitage — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/solarpunk-hermitage.html): Pitch 03 in the campgrounds. A wood cabin on wheels bristling with solar panels, and the first room on this street lit by daylight. A cave to read in, a campfire to watch from, a watering hole to make things at.
- [The Outskirts — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/the-outskirts.html): It's always dark in The Outskirts. The road past the last streetlight, where the mystical and the eldritch keep their own hours: hand-painted signs standing in the weeds, and only as much of them as the headlights reach.
- [Black Leather Lagoon — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/black-leather-lagoon.html): It's always Halloween at the Lagoon. A drive-in screen standing in black water at the edge of town, an appreciation of The Cramps, our Halloween playlist and a rack of their records on posts. Nothing plays until you press play, and nothing here flickers.
- [Sithen — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/sithen.html): A fairy fort seen from the outside, under a full moon. The rules nobody will say out loud, the ring that a whole country declines to plough, and a door this room does not open.
- [Looming Rocks Amphitheatre — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/looming-rocks.html): An open-air stage at the foot of enormous rock faces, after dark, with the lichen fluorescing under UV floods run off the day's sun. Whole concerts on the rocks, and nothing is fetched until you press something.
- [Dance, Punks — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/dance-punks.html): Turning 04 off The Outskirts: a silent disco on an old airstrip, lit by nothing but the headsets. Three channels in one crate of our dance-punk playlist, a headset each, and the volume in your own hand. Nothing strobes, and nothing plays until you put the headset on.
- [The Small Hours — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/small-hours.html): Turning 05 off The Outskirts: an all-night diner for bodies that keep other hours, seen lit from the dark car park. Crip time, a clock with no hands, breakfast whenever it is for you, crayons and a paper placemat to colour in, and nobody asking why you are up. On the jukebox, Josephmooon’s two albums, and Up All Night, a Stimpunk’s song about Autistic insomnia. It does not close, and it gives no sleep advice.
- [The Repeater — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/repeater.html): Turning 06 off The Outskirts: a radio mast on the ridge at the far end of the road, standing against the glow of everything else on it. Shared-signal space, a log that confirms every kind of contact and counts none, and a line you can leave open that goes nowhere and sends nothing.
- [Nothing For Sale — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/nothing-for-sale.html): Turning 07 off The Outskirts: a free market in a lay-by, lit by a ring of cars that pulled up nose-in and left their headlights on. Mutual aid rather than charity, tables of free things of ours, no proof of need, and nothing counted.
- [Liner Notes — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/liner-notes.html): Who made this noise. Every song, typeface, quotation and borrowed name on this street, credited to the person it belongs to.
- [Privacy — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/privacy.html): What this site knows about you, which is very little, and all of it: no cookies, a few things kept in your own browser, a CB that keeps one day of chat and nothing longer, nothing from anyone else until you press play, and our host's ordinary logs.
- [Changelog — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/changelog.html): What changed on the street, and when. Every Stimpunks site publishes one of these.
